claims.claim: IREN reported $4 billion of contracted ARR for 2026 capacity and $1 billion of operating ARR as of August 26, 2026, while AI Cloud Services revenue rose to $128.8 million in FY26 from $16.4 million in FY25.

IREN's 2026 capacity is largely sold out and Horizon 1 was delivered to Microsoft; the company also disclosed a broader customer set including hyperscalers, enterprises, AI developers and frontier labs.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: AI Cloud revenue expanded about eightfold year over year and operating ARR reached $1 billion, but consolidated FY26 net loss was $702.6 million and Q4 adjusted EBITDA fell amid platform investment.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Owned power, land, data centers, compute and software plus largely sold 2026 capacity indicate control of scarce power-to-compute infrastructure.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Customer diversification and contracted capacity reduce single-path demand risk, while rapid AI infrastructure buildout remains capital intensive and commissioning-dependent.

factors.name: catalystScore
factors.basis: The gap between $1 billion operating ARR and $4 billion contracted ARR creates a measurable commissioning and customer-acceptance catalyst through year-end 2026.

risks.risk: Contracted ARR is an operating metric rather than GAAP revenue and remains subject to commissioning, testing and customer acceptance; recognized revenue may be materially lower.
FY26 included $638.8 million of non-cash impairments primarily tied to decommissioning Bitcoin mining hardware, showing material transition cost and asset-obsolescence exposure.

unknowns.unknown: Scout did not establish independent current utilization or realized margin on the newly commissioned AI capacity; Alpha should not equate contracted ARR with realized revenue or earnings.

claims.claim: IREN disclosed $1 billion operating ARR versus $4 billion contracted ARR for 2026 capacity, making commissioning, testing and customer acceptance the central near-term execution bridge rather than demand contracting alone.

factors.name: expectationsExecution
factors.basis: Horizon 1 delivery and rapid AI revenue growth demonstrate execution, but most contracted ARR still depends on capacity becoming operational and accepted.

risks.risk: A delay in commissioning, testing or customer acceptance would widen the gap between contracted ARR and recognized GAAP revenue.

unknowns.unknown: Timing and economics of the remaining 2026 capacity acceptance are not yet fully realized in reported GAAP results.
